plan: Given my private value of $36, I aim to bid strategically to maximize profit. Other bidders are rational and likely bid close to their values. To win, I should bid slightly above the average expected value, around $24.5. However, to ensure a win and pay less, I will bid slightly below my value but above the average. This balances winning odds and potential profit.

Given my private value of $45, I aim to bid just below my value to maximize potential profit while considering the rational behavior of other bidders. Since values are uniformly distributed between $0 and $49, I expect others to bid close to their values. To balance winning chances and profit, I'll bid slightly below my value, say $43, to ensure a win if others bid closer to their values but not too high to minimize potential loss from the third-highest bid. This strategy optimizes my chance of winning while keeping costs manageable.

Given my private value of $49, I aim to win the auction while minimizing payment. Rational bidders will likely bid near their values. To maximize profit, I should bid slightly lower than my value, anticipating others bid below theirs to avoid overpaying. I expect bids around $24.5 (average value). Thus, I will bid $47 to secure victory, ensuring the third-highest bid is lower, maximizing my profit.
